record.issue_text: [BUG] The server-side dedupe against existing attendees is case-sensitive exact comparison (guest === attendee.email) while the blacklist check lowercases, so 'User@x.com' passes dedupe when 'user@x.com' is already an attendee. The same person is stored twice as a booking attendee, receives two ICS REQUEST emails, and is double-counted in calendar attendee updates; the client-side uniqueness check is trivially bypassed by any direct API caller.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server dedupe checks `guest === attendee.email` when filtering `uniqueGuests`, which is a case-sensitive comparison. Since `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` allows mixed-case emails (`z.string().email()` doesn’t normalize) and existing attendee emails may be stored in a different case, a caller can add `User@x.com` even if `user@x.com` is already an attendee, resulting in duplicate attendee records via `attendees.createMany`. The blacklist handling also lowercases only the blacklist entries but compares with the raw `guest`, so case variants can bypass the blacklist as well. This can lead to duplicated calendar attendee updates and duplicated email sends downstream.
